cards.headline: Pawlotsky 2015 (VITAL-1) — phase 2, interferon-free arms: SVR24 was 80–85% on alisporivir-based arms vs 58% on peginterferon/ribavirin; the 92% per-protocol figure is a response-selected reading, labelled as such
cards.summary: Pawlotsky 2015 (VITAL-1) — phase 2, interferon-free arms: SVR24 was 80–85% on alisporivir-based arms vs 58% on peginterferon/ribavirin; the 92% per-protocol figure is a response-selected reading, labelled as such
cards.type: Phase 2 randomised trial, VITAL-1 (Pawlotsky 2015) — report 3 of 3 in one programme, N = 1,880 across the programme
cards.people: 340 patients without cirrhosis, with treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis C genotype 2/3 infection, randomised to alisporivir 1,000 mg alone, alisporivir 600/800 mg plus ribavirin, alisporivir 600 mg plus peginterferon, or peginterferon/ribavirin; 300 patients received alisporivir-based regimens. Patients on interferon-free regimens who achieved rapid virological response continued unchanged; others added peginterferon from weeks 6–24.
cards.result: Intention-to-treat SVR24 was 80–85% across alisporivir arms vs 58% (23/40) on peginterferon/ribavirin. In the per-protocol analysis, patients who cleared virus early and stayed interferon-free on alisporivir/ribavirin achieved SVR24 in 92% (56/61) — a response-selected per-protocol reading, labelled as such. Viral breakthrough was infrequent (3%). Interferon-free alisporivir regimens showed markedly better safety/tolerability than interferon-containing regimens.
cards.watchOut: The 92% applies only to early clearers who stayed interferon-free — a subgroup defined by its own response. The intention-to-treat range (80–85%) is the quotable figure, against an obsolete comparator.
cards.source: Pawlotsky JM et al. Alisporivir plus ribavirin, interferon free or in combination with pegylated interferon, for hepatitis C virus genotype 2 or 3 infection. Hepatology. 2015. PMID: 26118427. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01215643. cards.headline: Synthesis
cards.summary: Synthesis
cards.people: One programme: 3 publications covering 3 trials, N = 1,880 randomised in total (1,081 + 459 + 340), plus one labelled harms-and-hold slice of the phase 3 report — never a fourth report. Alisporivir (development code DEB025) is an investigational drug that was never marketed for hepatitis C.
cards.result: Era flag (load-bearing): every trial is peginterferon-era (2015 reports of 2011–2013 trials); the comparator is obsolete, and the SVR contrasts measure alisporivir against a standard no longer used. Hold flag (load-bearing): a regulatory clinical hold truncated dosing in both genotype 1 trials, so even the positive SVR12 readings come from interrupted regimens; the programme was never resumed. The shelf's value is the host-targeting cyclophilin experiment and its fate, not a treatment option. The 90% (ESSENTIAL II) and 92% (VITAL-1) figures are duration-/response-selected subset readings and are never headline rates on this shelf.
cards.watchOut: Do not merge this shelf with the direct-acting antiviral shelves — alisporivir shares no anchor with any DAA home and asks the host-targeting question those shelves do not.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Bedside examination for ascites — FLOOR-RISK, exactly 2 reports: composite clinical evaluation strongly discriminative when suggestive, individual manoeuvres weak, overall accuracy 58% in the small referred study
shelves.question: In hospitalised patients with suspected ascites, how accurately do the bedside history and physical-examination findings — bulging flanks, flank dullness and its shifting, a fluid wave / thrill, peripheral oedema, and the patient's own report of increasing abdominal girth and weight gain — detect ascites against ultrasonography: what likelihood ratios did the prospective evaluation assign to each finding and to the overall clinical evaluation, and how accurate were the individual manoeuvres in the small referred-patient study in which only six patients actually had ascites? (FLOOR-RISK base: exactly 2 reports — one with N not documented in its abstract, one with N = 21 and only 6 positive cases.)
shelves.mesh: Ascites/complications,diagnosis · Humans · Male · Medical History Taking · Physical Examination · Probability · Prospective Studies · Ultrasonography
shelves.balance: FLOOR-RISK — this shelf rests on exactly 2 abstract-verifiable reports, and that exact basis prints here and on every card: a prospective evaluation whose abstract does not state its cohort size (N not documented) and a 21-patient referred study in which only 6 patients actually had ascites. The two reports disagree in register: the prospective evaluation finds the overall clinical evaluation powerfully discriminative (positive likelihood ratio 37.7–83.3 when suggestive, labelled as such) while individual manoeuvres are weak in both reports (overall accuracy only 58% in the small study), and no card converts the composite figure into a claim for any single sign. This is a diagnostic-accuracy shelf, not a treatment shelf.

cards.headline: FLOOR-RISK report 1 of exactly 2 — prospective evaluation of history and examination for ascites (Simel 1988, Journal of General Internal Medicine; cohort size not stated in the abstract: N not documented): the overall clinical evaluation produced a positive likelihood ratio of 37.7–83.3 when suggestive of ascites and 2.23–3.42 when intermediate, and a negative likelihood ratio of 0.77–0.90 when not suggestive (all labelled as such, ranges as published)
cards.summary: FLOOR-RISK report 1 of exactly 2 — prospective evaluation of history and examination for ascites (Simel 1988, Journal of General Internal Medicine; cohort size not stated in the abstract: N not documented): the overall clinical evaluation produced a positive likelihood ratio of 37.7–83.3 when suggestive of ascites and 2.23–3.42 when intermediate, and a negative likelihood ratio of 0.77–0.90 when not suggestive (all labelled as such, ranges as published)
cards.type: Prospective evaluation of operating characteristics (FLOOR-RISK report 1 of exactly 2; N not documented in the abstract)
cards.people: A broad spectrum of hospitalised patients, prospectively evaluated; the abstract does not state the cohort size — N not documented, printed as such. Report 1 of exactly 2 on this FLOOR-RISK shelf.
cards.result: Individual findings (likelihood ratios labelled as such): fluid wave positive likelihood ratio 9.6; shifting dullness 5.76; reported increased abdominal girth 4.16; recent weight gain 3.20. Absence of subjective ankle swelling (negative likelihood ratio 0.10) and of increased girth (0.17) best lowered the probability; absence of bulging flanks gave a negative likelihood ratio of 0.12 and absence of peripheral oedema 0.17. The authors conclude a routine history and physical examination are quantitatively useful in the clinical evaluation of ascites.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 reports form this shelf's whole base. The strong figures belong to the overall clinical evaluation, not to any single manoeuvre — never convert the composite positive likelihood ratio (up to 83.3) into a claim for fluid wave, shifting dullness or any other single sign.
cards.source: Simel DL et al. Quantitating bedside diagnosis: clinical evaluation of ascites. Journal of general internal medicine. 1988. PMID: 3049966. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: FLOOR-RISK report 2 of exactly 2 — accuracy of the physical examination in suspected ascites (Cattau 1982, JAMA — 21 patients referred with questionable ascites, only 6 of whom had ascites on ultrasonography): manoeuvre sensitivity ranged 50–94% and specificity 29–82%, overall accuracy was only 58%, and the single >90%-accurate conclusion was that ascites is absent if no flank dullness is elicited
cards.summary: FLOOR-RISK report 2 of exactly 2 — accuracy of the physical examination in suspected ascites (Cattau 1982, JAMA — 21 patients referred with questionable ascites, only 6 of whom had ascites on ultrasonography): manoeuvre sensitivity ranged 50–94% and specificity 29–82%, overall accuracy was only 58%, and the single >90%-accurate conclusion was that ascites is absent if no flank dullness is elicited
cards.type: Accuracy study in referred patients (FLOOR-RISK report 2 of exactly 2; N = 21, only 6 with ascites)
cards.people: 21 patients referred for evaluation with a diagnosis of questionable ascites, examined independently by three investigators performing five physical-examination manoeuvres; ultrasonography as reference standard; only 6 patients had ascites. Report 2 of exactly 2 on this FLOOR-RISK shelf.
cards.result: Sensitivity and specificity of the manoeuvres ranged from 50% to 94% and 29% to 82% respectively; overall accuracy was only 58%. The only conclusion a physical manoeuvre could make with over 90% accuracy was that ascites is absent if no flank dullness is elicited. The authors conclude routine physical examination has definite limitations in precise diagnosis of equivocal ascites and recommend ultrasonography in questionable cases.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK: with only 6 positive cases, every sensitivity figure in this report rests on a handful of patients — printed wherever its figures appear. This report's weak register (58% overall accuracy) stands beside, and is not averaged away by, the prospective evaluation's strong composite figures.

cards.headline: Cross-report summary of the two carded FLOOR-RISK reports — not an additional report (source line repeats report 1 for reference): the composite clinical evaluation looks powerful in the prospective evaluation while individual manoeuvres are weak in both reports, and the small referred study's overall accuracy was only 58%

cards.people: The two carded reports only: Simel 1988 (prospective evaluation, N not documented in its abstract) and Cattau 1982 (N = 21, 6 with ascites). This card adds no report and no data.
cards.result: Read together: history items (increased girth, weight gain, ankle swelling) and the overall clinical impression carry most of the discriminative weight in the prospective evaluation (composite positive likelihood ratio 37.7–83.3 when suggestive, labelled as such), whereas no individual manoeuvre in either report is both sensitive and specific, and in referred equivocal cases the examination's overall accuracy was 58% with ultrasonography recommended. The disagreement in register between the two reports is content, not noise.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK basis restated: exactly 2 reports — one with N not documented, one with N = 21 and only 6 positive cases. Nothing on this shelf rests on any third report.

shelves.title: Asimadoline for irritable bowel syndrome pain — FLOOR-RISK: exactly 2 efficacy reports, N = 696, both ITT primaries null
shelves.question: In adults with irritable bowel syndrome, does oral asimadoline (0.15–1.0 mg twice daily for 12 weeks, or on-demand dosing for pain episodes) versus placebo increase adequate relief of IBS pain/discomfort or reduce episode pain severity?
shelves.mesh: Abdominal Pain/drug therapy · Acetamides/therapeutic use · Adolescent · Adult · Aged · Dose-Response Relationship, Drug · Double-Blind Method · Female · Gastrointestinal Agents/therapeutic use · Humans · Irritable Bowel Syndrome/drug therapy · Male · Middle Aged · Pyrrolidines/therapeutic use · Receptors, Opioid, kappa/therapeutic use · Treatment Outcome · Anxiety/drug therapy · Depression/drug therapy · Irritable Bowel Syndrome/drug therapy/psychology · Pain Measurement · Quality of Life · Receptors, Opioid, kappa/agonists
shelves.balance: MAYBE (weak evidence) — FLOOR-RISK, stated exactly: exactly 2 efficacy reports, total N = 696 (596 + 100), and BOTH missed their intention-to-treat primary endpoints. The adequately powered trial (n = 596) was null at every dose in the ITT population; its positive readings live in a diarrhoea-predominant subgroup with at least moderate baseline pain at a single dose (0.5 mg) and in the alternating-IBS subgroup — subgroup readings from a null trial. The on-demand trial (100 women only) was likewise null on its primary, with post-hoc, unadjusted readings pointing in OPPOSITE directions by subtype (mixed IBS p = .003; diarrhoea-predominant p = .065, towards worse). A colonic-distension mechanistic crossover study exists in the programme and is fenced off — a physiology experiment, never counted as an efficacy report; the functional-dyspepsia and healthy-volunteer satiation studies ask different questions and are not counted. No phase 3 programme followed for IBS. Asimadoline is an investigational drug that was never marketed for IBS (clarification, not promotion). The shelf presents a tested-and-failed visceral-analgesic strategy whose mechanistic premise was stronger than its clinical results. It must never be merged with fedotozine into a κ-opioid class row.

cards.headline: Mangel 2008 (report 1 of exactly 2): the phase 2b primary endpoint was NOT significant in the intention-to-treat population at any dose
cards.summary: Mangel 2008 (report 1 of exactly 2): the phase 2b primary endpoint was NOT significant in the intention-to-treat population at any dose
cards.type: Report 1 of exactly 2 efficacy reports — double-blind randomised placebo-controlled phase 2b trial (12 weeks)
cards.people: 596 patients randomised to asimadoline 0.15, 0.5 or 1.0 mg or placebo twice daily for 12 weeks.
cards.result: The primary endpoint (months of adequate relief of IBS pain or discomfort) was not statistically significant in the intention-to-treat population. Asimadoline was well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: The trial's positive readings are confined to subgroups and are carded separately below, labelled as subgroup readings of a null trial — they do not change the ITT result.

cards.summary: Szarka 2007 (labelled post-hoc slice of report 2 of exactly 2, never a second report): post-hoc readings pointed in opposite directions by subtype (mixed IBS p = .003; diarrhoea-predominant p = .065 towards worse) — both unadjusted

cards.people: The same 100-woman on-demand trial carded above; this slice reports its post-hoc subtype readings only.

cards.headline: Synthesis: asimadoline for IBS pain — MAYBE (weak evidence) on an exact-2, both-null base (N = 696)
cards.summary: Synthesis: asimadoline for IBS pain — MAYBE (weak evidence) on an exact-2, both-null base (N = 696)
cards.people: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional population.
cards.result: Exactly 2 efficacy reports, total N = 696, both intention-to-treat primaries null. The only positive readings are a single-dose subgroup of the larger trial and unadjusted post-hoc subtype readings of the smaller trial that point in opposite directions. A mechanistic colonic-distension study in the programme is programme context only and was never counted. No phase 3 programme followed; asimadoline was never marketed for IBS.
cards.watchOut: FLOOR-RISK: if the exact count (2 reports, N = 696) cannot be verified from the face, this shelf should not be relied on — the count is the finding. Never average the subgroup positives over the null primaries.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.
